title: How to remove OpenCode session spawning while preserving csm-orchestrate goals

tldr.content: Replace the CLI child-process host with an explicit in-process SkillExecutor registry. Do not use the OpenCode SDK as a substitute: its documented createOpencode() starts an OpenCode server and client, which preserves the unwanted runtime dependency. [ref-sdk]

executiveSummary.content: The repository already has the correct control-plane seam: orchestrate() accepts host.invokeSiblingSkill(request, { signal }). The missing piece is a real execution plane. OpenCode's SDK/server documentation confirms that its programmatic API still creates or connects to OpenCode sessions, so it is unsuitable for the stated no-OpenCode-session goal. [ref-local-host] [ref-sdk]

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported: The current process launch is isolated to the optional CLI host, not the core orchestrator. [ref-local-host]

K2. supported: The shipped CLI host defaults to opencode run and therefore creates nested OpenCode execution. [ref-local-host]

K3. supported: The repository has metadata but no general executable sibling registry. [ref-local-registry]

K4. supported: OpenCode's official SDK starts a server/client or connects to an existing server and exposes session APIs; it does not provide a direct call into this repository's skill functions. [ref-sdk] [ref-server]

K5. recommended: A typed in-process registry is the smallest architecture that removes OpenCode while retaining the existing validation, approvals, receipts, evidence, retry, and recovery control plane. [ref-local-invocation] [ref-idempotency]

detail-sections.content:
Recommended boundary:

User/host -> orchestrate() -> policy and durable control plane -> SkillExecutor registry -> typed skill handler -> child result/evidence

The registry should be separate from capabilities.json. Each handler should declare a stable skill ID, input schema, output/receipt schema, cancellation behavior, artifact ownership, and whether it is read-only or side-effecting. The orchestrator should resolve the handler by exact skill ID and digest, reject missing handlers, and never fall back to an LLM or CLI.

Handlers can initially wrap existing callable libraries such as csm-ddd's analyzeRepository() and csm-scan's runExpandedPipeline(). Instruction-only skills such as csm-plan, csm-build, csm-review, and csm-deep-research need typed runtime entrypoints before they can be executed in-process; otherwise they must remain explicitly unsupported. [ref-local-registry]

Retries remain at-least-once. Persist the natural idempotency key and prior response before acknowledging completion, following the idempotent-receiver pattern. [ref-idempotency]

recommendation.content: Recommend removing createCliHost() from the default/public path and adding a first-party in-process executor registry. Do not replace it with @opencode-ai/sdk, because that still starts or connects to an OpenCode server and manages OpenCode sessions. Pilot the registry with csm-ddd and csm-scan, then convert other skills one at a time to typed callable handlers; route unsupported skills to a typed BLOCKED result. Success requires zero OpenCode process launches, complete child receipt/evidence lineage, cancellation, retry idempotency, independent final review, and durable restart tests. [ref-sdk] [ref-server] [ref-local-registry]

unverified-claims.content:
1. The repository's intended production caller is not present in this checkout; verify the external integration that currently constructs createCliHost().
2. Direct callable entrypoints were confirmed for representative skills, not every skill. Inventory and type-check each handler before enabling it.
3. The exact final-review implementation should be chosen after deciding whether review is a local deterministic validator or a separately hosted reviewer; do not weaken independence by placing both roles in one handler.

process-appendix.content: Strategy: STANDARD, hybrid. Local tracks covered goals/control-plane, host execution, and registry feasibility; web sources covered OpenCode SDK/server semantics and idempotent retry design. Independent code-reading agents challenged the host-path and registry conclusions. No repository code was executed or modified. Recommendation confidence is high for the architectural direction and medium for the exact handler inventory. The research does not authorize implementation.
